html:
Spanish painter and sculptor, born in Málaga in 1881, who worked mostly in France. He co-founded Cubism and painted Guernica, and is one of the most influential artists of the 1900s.

He settled in Paris in 1904. His early work went through a Blue Period and a Rose Period. In 1907 he painted Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, five nude women with mask like faces. With Georges Braque he then developed Cubism, breaking objects into flat planes seen from many angles at once.

In 1937, during the Spanish Civil War, German and Italian planes bombed the Basque town of Guernica. Picasso answered with Guernica, a huge black and white painting of screaming people and animals, shown at the Paris World's Fair. It became one of the most famous protests against war. He would not let it go to Spain while Franco ruled; it went there only in 1981.

He worked in every medium, from ceramics to collage, and kept changing styles until his death in the south of France in 1973.
